title: Generation of $N$-particle kappa-distributed velocities via superstatistical Gibbs sampling
abstract: The \emph{kappa} distribution is widely used to model heavy-tailed, non-equilibrium velocity distributions in space and laboratory plasmas. Its correct use in particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations requires more than sampling the single-particle marginal: the $N$-particle \emph{kappa} distribution predicts non-trivial correlations between the kinetic energies of particles. Building on the superstatistical structure, we implement a Gibbs sampler whose stationary distribution is the joint distribution of the velocities and $β$, so that the sampled velocities follow the $N$-particle \emph{kappa} distribution and reproduce these correlations by construction.
summary: This work develops a specialized Gibbs sampling algorithm to generate $N$-particle velocity distributions that correctly follow the kappa distribution, which is crucial for simulating non-equilibrium plasmas. By sampling the joint distribution of velocities and the superstatistical parameter $ eta$, the method successfully reproduces non-trivial correlations between particle kinetic energies that independent sampling methods miss.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately generating $N$-particle kappa-distributed velocities, which are necessary for simulating non-equilibrium plasmas, because the joint distribution does not factorize into independent single-particle marginals.
main_result: A Gibbs sampler was successfully implemented that reproduces the full joint $N$-particle kappa distribution, correctly capturing non-trivial correlations between particle kinetic energies.
method: The authors employed a Gibbs sampling Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method, alternating between sampling velocities from a Maxwellian conditional and sampling the inverse temperature $ eta$ from a Gamma conditional.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a plasma described by a superstatistical framework where the velocity distribution follows the kappa distribution. This distribution is treated as a mixture weighted by a probability distribution for the inverse temperature $ eta$.
key_observables: Mean kinetic energy, Pearson correlation coefficient ($ho$), and Mutual Information ($I_{k_1, k_2}$) for two-particle kinetic energies.
important_parameters: The plasma parameter $\kappa$ (via the superstatistical structure) and the variance parameter $u$ governing the superstatistics.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the joint $N$-particle distribution structure must be explicitly sampled because single-particle marginals are insufficient; furthermore, the variance of the correlation estimator requires $u < 1/4$.
figures_summary: Figures compare sampled velocity histograms against the exact kappa distribution for varying $u$, show the recovered distribution of $ eta$ vs. theory, and illustrate the recovery of joint kinetic energy distributions and correlation measures.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework for the joint $N$-particle kappa distribution, implements the Gibbs sampler based on conditional distributions, and then validates the sampler by comparing sampled observables (like $\langle k angle$, $ho$, and $I$) against analytical predictions across varying parameters.
why_interesting: While focused on plasma physics, the rigorous application of superstatistics and advanced MCMC techniques to model non-equilibrium, correlated many-body systems is highly relevant to understanding complex dynamics in quantum many-body systems where simple product states fail.
